record.original_question: Which foliations with affine leaves can be described as the ima ge of the moment map? Notice that a similar problem is still open even in the symplectic setting: which closed manifolds Bn may serve as bases of locally trivial Lagrangian fibrations M 2n T n - → Bn, where M 2n is symplectic? Extensions of the affine structure to the singular setting are also d esirable. One instance when the affine structure on the leaves extends to an affine structure on th e image of the moment map for non-regular Poisson manifolds is the case of b-Poisson manifolds [107]. For these manifolds this affine structure is well-understood and classified via the Delzant theorem [106]. Such a phenomenon is also observed for other Poisson structures with open dense leaves on bm-Poisson manifolds [104].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a connected symplectic manifold and let $\pi: M^{2n} \to B^n$ be a locally trivial Lagrangian fibration over a closed $n$-dimensional manifold $B^n$, with fiber the standard $n$-torus $T^n$ (so each fiber $\pi^{-1}(b)$ is a Lagrangian submanifold diffeomorphic to $T^n$, and $\pi$ is locally trivial in the smooth category). The Arnold–Liouville theorem endows $B^n$ with an integral affine structure.

Problem. Characterize the closed $n$-manifolds $B^n$ that arise in this way: give necessary and sufficient conditions on a closed smooth manifold $B^n$ for the existence of a symplectic manifold $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ and a locally trivial Lagrangian $T^n$-fibration $\pi: M^{2n} \to B^n$.

(Equivalent reformulation: classify the closed $n$-manifolds that admit an integral affine structure for which the associated $T^n$-bundle carries a symplectic form making the projection a Lagrangian fibration.)
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of closed manifolds that can serve as bases of locally trivial Lagrangian torus fibrations of symplectic manifolds is described in recent surveys and lecture notes (e.g., Evans' lectures on Lagrangian torus fibrations, 2021) as an open problem. Partial results exist (e.g., constraints from integral affine structures, results on tori, and in the hyperkähler setting Matsushita/Hwang's results forcing the smooth base to be projective space), but no full classification is known.

status_evidence.title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 6.6 explicitly states this question remains open in the symplectic setting.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Lectures on Lagrangian torus fibrations (arXiv:2110.08643)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of locally trivial Lagrangian torus fibrations and the structure of their bases as integral affine manifolds, with classification questions remaining open.
status_evidence.claim: Full classification of admissible base manifolds is not given; the question is treated as open.
